topic: Introducing Cane Toads to Eat Beetles Made Australia Toxic to Predators
research_summary: In 1935 the Queensland Bureau of Sugar Experiment Stations imported ~100 cane toads (Rhinella marina) from Hawaii, bred them, and released ~2,400 offspring near Gordonvale to control root-feeding scarab cane beetles — without prior study of environmental impact or of whether toads could even reach the beetles, which fed high on cane stalks out of the ground-dwelling toads' reach. The biocontrol failed at its stated purpose while the toads spread across northern Australia (now moving ~40-60 km/yr, accelerated by invasion-front toads evolving longer legs). The toads carry bufadienolide/bufotoxin cardiac glycosides in parotoid glands; naive Australian predators (northern quolls, freshwater crocodiles, varanid goannas, large elapid snakes) that had never co-evolved with bufonids die when they attempt to eat toads, causing severe population declines — the 'toxic to predators' outcome. Some predators and prey have shown behavioural (conditioned taste aversion) and rapid evolutionary responses (snakes evolving larger bodies/smaller relative gape; black snakes evolving tolerance). Comparable biocontrol/invasion cases: the small Indian mongoose introduced to Hawaii (1883) to control cane-field rats, which failed (diurnal vs nocturnal mismatch) and devastated native ground-nesting birds; Cactoblastis cactorum, a genuine biocontrol success against prickly pear in Australia that became destructive when it reached native cacti in North America; the predatory snail Euglandina rosea driving Pacific land-snail extinctions; and cane toads killing endemic Jamaican boas in the West Indies. Sources prioritise the National Museum of Australia, DCCEEW, peer-reviewed open-access papers (Nature, Conservation Science and Practice, PMC/PubMed, biorxiv, USDA Forest Service, int-res.com, Oxford Academic), and Hawaiian/US government agencies. Some authoritative papers sit behind publisher paywalls (ScienceDirect, some Wiley portals) and are flagged/avoided as support-quote risks where possible. Deliberate over-provisioning of ~57 claims budgets for retrieval attrition (paywalls, quotes not on page).
